quarterly_data.signal: AI transformation is moving into the storage layer — total data-center NAND bits this year exceed PC + mobile combined; rising adoption of higher-layer-count QLC NAND for SSDs. The ~$40B NAND conversion (to >200-layer) is being PULLED FORWARD, with the majority of spending now before end of CY2027; industry installed wafer capacity expected to decline >20% from prior highs by year-end, driving greenfield investment; industry converting to 256-layer-and-above class devices. Lam has the largest installed base of 3D-NAND tools and leadership in high-aspect-ratio cryo etch, dielectric-stack deposition, metallization, backside-stress and gap-fill.
quarterly_data.figure: $40B NAND conversion pulled forward to pre-2028; 256-layer+; capacity -20%

quarterly_data.signal: Structural NAND supply gap: industry installed wafer capacity will be DOWN MORE THAN 20% from prior highs by end of 2026 — so on top of the pulled-forward $40B 200+-layer conversion (majority spent before end of CY2027), bit-demand growth should force GREENFIELD capacity investment. Data-center NAND bits this year expected to exceed PC and mobile segments COMBINED. Lam holds the largest 3D-NAND installed base; mid-ramp conductor-etch win (customer switched tools mid-production for yield) shows tools being chosen for output in a capacity-constrained environment.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND wafer capacity -20%+ from peak by end-2026; greenfield investment ahead

NAND sourcing is a moat: 2026 supply allocations were finalized by flash makers by MID-2025, and Silicon Motion secures NAND from 3 different makers; NAND vendors are retreating from edge/client segments (PC units now seen -10%+ in 2026, smartphones -10%+) to prioritize enterprise/cloud AI — accelerating controller outsourcing share gains.
